result.title: Specification-Guided Generation for Large Language Models
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can generate structured outputs, but existing constrained-decoding methods mainly enforce syntax and cannot directly enforce satisfaction of a formal specification. We introduce a neuro-symbolic, specification-guided decoding framework that combines LLM generation with symbolic reasoning. At each step, the framework refines the decoding grammar by filtering out values that cannot be extended to an output satisfying the specification. We present a forward-only variant that guarantees specification satisfaction by construction, and a backtracking variant that revises earlier feasible choices when their downstream consequences leave only values that the LLM itself judges unsuitable. The framework is model-agnostic, requires no retraining, and builds on existing grammar-constrained decoding mechanisms. Experiments on configuration and constraint-solving benchmarks show that the forward-only variant reliably produces specification-compliant outputs while reducing repeated LLM inference compared with rejection sampling and incurring modest symbolic-reasoning overhead. The backtracking variant further reduces cases in which the model is forced to select values that it has itself judged unsuitable, thereby substantially improving adherence to the LLM's stated interpretation of the prompt.

AI.brief_summary: 提出神经符号的规范引导解码框架：每一步用符号推理过滤无法扩展为满足形式规范的候选值，给出前向保证版与回溯修正版，并在配置与约束求解基准上验证合规性与开销。
AI.relevance_reason: 逐步可行性过滤与「下游后果不佳时回退早期选择」的机制，可能为 latent 推理中的状态验证、错误步骤回退与停止决策提供线索；但纯文本约束解码与视觉 latent 状态之间的距离仍需核查。
